declarations.docstring: Taking inverses of the unit parameter gives the inverse auxiliary coordinate element.
A dual basis vector has the negation of the displayed auxiliary weight.
Distinct integer exponents can be separated by powers of a unit in a characteristic-zero field.
The dual auxiliary weight space has the dimension of the space indexed by the negated weight.
The dimension of an auxiliary weight space is counted by basis vectors with that weight.
Under the stated spanning condition, a dual auxiliary-polynomial coefficient is the dimension at the opposite weight.
The auxiliary space indexed by natural weights agrees with its integer-indexed counterpart.
